# situation: on issues, a job whose token may write contents echoes the
#   issue's title, written in by ${{ }}.
# reason: issues runs the job for anyone who opens an issue, with no
#   approval, and contents: write gives its token write; the title written
#   in by ${{ }} is a flaw that runs the opener's code in the job that holds
#   that token.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
# attack-run-behavior: opening the issue starts the job a, which has no if
#   and waits for no approval, with a token that has contents: write; the
#   script becomes echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "", and the shell runs echo
#   PWNED as a command, so any command the attacker writes in its place runs
#   in the job that holds that token.
on: workflow_call
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
